stem: Which finding on a serial head circumference chart would raise significant suspicion for raised intracranial pressure in a child?

options.text: Measurements that cross percentile lines upward
Measurements that remain steady on the $50^{th}$ percentile
A single measurement taken at the onset of the headache
Measurements that cross percentile lines downward

explanation: Crossing percentile lines indicates a rate of head growth that is disproportionate, suggesting increased internal pressure.
rationale: Look for a trend that suggests the head size is increasing faster than the standard growth curve.

optionExplanations.A: Crossing percentile lines indicates a rate of head growth that is disproportionate, suggesting increased internal pressure.
optionExplanations.B: Consistency along a percentile line usually indicates normal, expected growth.
optionExplanations.C: Serial measurements are necessary to determine if there is a concerning trend over time.
optionExplanations.D: Downward crossing might indicate failure to thrive or microcephaly, but not typically raised intracranial pressure.
